other/2026-09-18-owl-setup.title: Owl Setup
other/2026-09-18-owl-setup.content:
Getting on the owls
I emailed Unni and did this as a part of getting a UiO account. Taken from the Component Separation Course:
Once you have received a username and password for your UiO account, you should log in and check that everything works before the workshop. Here are some instructions:
First you need to set up two-factor authentication (2FA) as decribed here:
www.uio.no/english/services/it/username-password/2fa/help/enable-2fa-qr.html
After this, open a Linux terminal, and log in to the ITA login node:
ssh -l <your username> login.astro.uio.no
At this point, as long as you’re outside of the UiO internet/Wifi, you will be asked for a 2FA code, which you should now be able to do if you have set it up. After you have logged in to the login node, you can set up a ssh key pair (there are tons of guides for how to do this online, for example this: www.howtogeek.com/424510/how-to-create-and-install-ssh-keys-from-the-linux-shell/). Even with a key pair, however, you still need to give your 2FA code as long as you’re working remotely.
From the login node, you can then access the owl cluster. The owl cluster is a bunch of machines that have names like owlxx.uio.no, where xx is a number from 39 to 46 when you want enough memory for a large commander run.
ssh owlxx.uio.no
Now you should be logged in to the owl and you can set up a similar ssh-keypair here so that you don’t have to provide your personal password each time.
Compilers etc are available through the module system. To see what is available, type:
module avail
We dont have any queuing system on the nodes, just be polite :) You can get an overview over available owls to run on here:
astro-clusters.uio.no/
Setting up python
I followed this link to set up python. It didn’t work directly but with some AI troubleshooting it did. Ultimately, it added these lines to my .bashrc:
# >>> mamba initialize >>>
# !! Contents within this block are managed by 'mamba shell init' !!
export MAMBA_EXE='/mn/stornext/astro/local/mamba/bin/mamba';
export MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX='/mn/stornext/astro/local/mamba';
__mamba_setup="$("$MAMBA_EXE" shell hook --shell bash --root-prefix "$MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX" 2> /dev/null)"
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    eval "$__mamba_setup"
else
    alias mamba="$MAMBA_EXE"  # Fallback on help from mamba activate
fi
unset __mamba_setup
# <<< mamba initialize <<<
 
mamba activate py312

other/2026-09-21-gpt-uio-setup.title: Getting GPT UiO setup with API Keys
other/2026-09-21-gpt-uio-setup.content:
Overview
The university provides a free AI service called GPT UiO. It’s not terribly good, but free is better than not free! Best of all, it can be incorporated into VSCode or other IDE platforms.
The service is described here : GPT UiO.
There are dozens of models. From my quick digging, it seems that the best as of writing this (updated Nov 2026) are GLM 5.3 for coding and GPT 6.1 Sol for general work (GPT 6.1 Terra is a slightly lighter, newer alternative). They also specify a security level on each model. This is not something I am too interested in personally, but it is there if you are.
There are two steps to set this up:

Get API key access from the university
Add them to VSCode.

Note: there are many ways to do this, but this method uses the github copilot harness to feed queries, and therefore is a drop-in replacement for the default copilot’s chat feature. It will be able to get context from your repository automatically, see what file you have open, and what lines you have highlighted. But this won’t be the model that does inline ghost-text completion.
Getting the API keys
This service is described here: getting API keys.
Email gpt-drift@usit.uio.no and provide:

Your UiO email/username
Say that you are requesting API keys
What you plan to use them for (I said a sentence or two here)

Now when you visit gpt.uio.no, you will have access to the My API keys option in the dropdown menu available from clicking your name.

Plugging the models into VSCode
This only took a few minutes once the keys were issued:


Log in to gpt.uio.no, click your username in the top right, and open My API keys. Hit Generate new. There is one key for yellow-data and one for red-data models. I made one for each, but I only use the yellow-data models anyways.


Click on the model you want. You will need the Key, Base URL, and Model it lists. The Key is shared between all models in the same category, so there is a red key and a yellow key.


In VSCode, open the Chat tab (ctrl + cmd + i), click the Models button at the bottom left, and press the plus icon next to Copilot:



A Language Models window will pop up. Click Add Models and then click Custom Endpoint in the dropdown:


Type “GPT UiO (yellow)” as the model group, if you are installing a yellow-data endpoint.
Copy paste the API key for yellow data that you got in step 2.
Click “Responses” as the API type.



A chatLanguageModels.json file will pop up. Don’t be afraid, we are almost done! You need to fill out the “id”, “name”, and “url”:

The “id” is from step 2, called the “Model” on the GPT UiO website. It is important to get this exactly right, so copy/paste it.
The “name” is anything you want it to be. It is the name for this particular model.
The “url” is from step 2 also, just gpt.uio.no/api/v1.

When you are done, it should look like this:



Done! You should be able to click the model below your Copilot chat and start using it.

This should have all the access to your code that Copilot has because it uses Copilot’s harness. It should be able to ask you questions as it runs, see what file you have open and which lines are highlighted, etc.


To add more models:


To add another yellow model, open the Language Models window again (open the Chat tab (ctrl + cmd + i), click the Models button, and press the plus icon). Then click on the gear icon on the far right and press Add Model:

Then fill out the chatLanguageModels.json like you did before with the second model. When you are done, your chatLanguageModels.json should look like:



To add a red model, repeat steps 2–5 with the red-data key and a red model. Call this model group “GPT UiO (red)”. Everything else is the same.
